step1_analysis.description: A basic PMOS current mirror that replicates a reference current. Given the paper's focus on micropower and subthreshold operation, it is likely used to distribute small bias currents across the cochlear chip.

paper_reference.title: A 126-W Cochlear Chip for a Totally Implantable System

current_ratio.description: Ratio of the mirrored output current to the input reference current.

sky130_expected.calculation: Iout / Iref. With Vout=0.9V and Vref~1.32V, channel length modulation increases Iout slightly. Ratio = (1 + 0.1*0.9) / (1 + 0.1*0.48) ≈ 1.04
sky130_expected.reasoning: Ideal ratio is 1.0 since W/L are identical, but finite output resistance and different Vds voltages cause a slight systematic error.

output_resistance.description: Small-signal output resistance of the mirror.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the channel length modulation parameter (lambda) for L=0.5um in SKY130.

power_consumption.description: Total power consumed by the current mirror.

paper_reported.value: 126 uW (chip total, OCR typo in title)

sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on a 1uA reference current, which places the transistors in moderate/weak inversion as typical for micropower cochlear applications.

step3_testbench.description: DC sweep of the output voltage to measure current ratio, output resistance, and power consumption.
step3_testbench.spice:
* PMOS Current Mirror Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u

XM4 N0 N0 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N3 N0 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
Iref N0 0 1u
* Voltage source to set Vout and measure Iout
Vout N3 0 0.9

.control
  * Sweep output voltage to measure output resistance
  dc Vout 0 1.8 0.01
  
  * Measure currents at different output voltages
  meas dc iout_08 find i(Vout) at=0.8
  meas dc iout_10 find i(Vout) at=1.0
  meas dc iout_nom find i(Vout) at=0.9
  meas dc ivdd_nom find i(VVDD) at=0.9
  
  * Calculate metrics
  * Note: i(Vout) decreases as Vout increases (Vds becomes less negative), so iout_08 > iout_10
  let rout = 0.2 / (iout_08 - iout_10)
  let current_ratio = iout_nom / 1u
  let power = -ivdd_nom * 1.8
  
  print rout current_ratio power
  quit
.endc
